title: Sequences of Real Numbers
description: Module 1 — theorem structure, subsequences, and completeness

edges.label: for \(a_n=ar^{n-1}\), the ratio \(a_{n+1}/a_n\) is the constant ___
edges.hint: Compute one quotient of consecutive terms.

edges.label: in the epsilon-N definition, for all \(n>N\) we require \(|a_n-L|\) ___ \(\varepsilon\)
edges.hint: Convergence requires \(a_n\) to get closer to \(L\)

edges.label: A sequence is called divergent if
edges.answer: for all \(L\), there exists \(\epsilon>0\) such that \(\forall N\), there exists \(n>N\) such that \(|a_n - L| >\epsilon\)
options: for all \(L\), for all \(\epsilon>0\), \(\exists N\) such that if \(n>N\) then \(|a_n - L| >\epsilon\)
for all \(L\), there exists \(\epsilon>0\) such that \(\forall N\), if \(n>N\) then \(|a_n - L| >\epsilon\)
for all \(L\), there exists \(\epsilon>0\) such that \(\forall N\), there exists \(n>N\) such that \(|a_n - L| >\epsilon\)
for all \(L\), there exists \(\epsilon>0\) such that \(\exists N\) such that for all \(n>N\), we have \(|a_n - L| >\epsilon\)
edges.hint: Negate the standard definition

edges.label: a convergent sequence has how many limits?
edges.hint: Limit is unique in \(\mathbb{R}\).

edges.label: if \(a_n\to a\) and \(b_n\to b\), then \(a_n+b_n\to\) ___
edges.hint: Use the sum law for limits.

edges.label: if \(a_n\le b_n\) eventually and both converge, then \(\lim a_n\) ___ \(\lim b_n\)
edges.hint: Limit inequalities preserve weak order.

edges.label: removing finitely many initial terms ___ the limit
edges.hint: Convergence depends on tail behavior.

edges.label: if the outer sequences both tend to \(L\), then the trapped middle sequence also tends to ___
edges.hint: The outer bounds force the same limit.

edges.label: which statement is the correct formal meaning of boundedness for a sequence?
edges.answer: |a_n| ≤ M for some M and all n
options: |a_n| ≤ M for some M and all n
edges.hint: Boundedness means all terms stay inside one fixed interval centered at 0.

edges.label: every convergent real sequence is bounded: true or false?
edges.hint: The tail is near \(L\), and finitely many initial terms are bounded too.

edges.label: in the nondecreasing case, monotonicity means \(a_{n+1}\) ___ \(a_n\)
edges.hint: This edge checks the order relation, not the vocabulary word.

edges.label: a subsequence uses strictly ___ indices \(n_1 < n_2 < \cdots\)
edges.hint: You can skip terms, but you cannot go backward.

edges.label: if some extracted terms \(a_{n_k}\) converge to \(L\), then \(L\) is the limit of a ___
edges.hint: The extracted indices \(n_k\) define the smaller sequence whose limit is \(L\).

edges.label: if \(a_n \to L\), then every subsequence also converges to ___
edges.hint: Passing to a subsequence does not change the tail limit.

edges.label: if the even and odd subsequences approach different numbers, the original sequence is:
edges.hint: A convergent sequence cannot have two different subsequential limits.

edges.label: if \(a_n\to L\), Cesàro means satisfy \(\sigma_n\to\) ___
edges.hint: Averaging preserves the limit in this direction.

edges.label: an index \(n\) is a peak point if no later term is ___ than \(a_n\)
edges.hint: A peak is a skyline maximum among all later terms.

edges.label: the peak/no-peak dichotomy guarantees a subsequence that is either nonincreasing or ___
edges.hint: The lemma produces a monotone subsequence in one of the two order directions.

edges.label: a subsequential limit is also an ___ point of the set of sequence values
edges.hint: Equivalent terminology: cluster point.
